review_comments.body:
** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Continue counters generated during the current lookup.** If `report(999).pdf` and `report(1000).pdf` are taken, the loop next tries `report(1000)(1).pdf` instead of `report(1001).pdf`. Near the 255-character limit, the nested suffix causes a length error even when `(1001).pdf` would fit. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/infiniflow/ragflow/49f18d03f02fa9e6021f9ef24f41ca64fce7e493/internal/common/app_name.go)) Parse the input once and increment the generated counter separately. Add a collision test across the 999-to-1000 boundary.

Keeps years intact, as years should shine.
When one is taken, adds `(1)`,
Then hops along beneath the sun.
The suffix rules are clear and neat,

Thanks — reporter of #22162 here. Verified the defect on main @ eeeda3604 with a test-only repro (carried in the issue body): `splitNameCounter("report(2023)")` returned `("report", 2023, true)` and `UniqueFileName` renamed a colliding upload to `report(2024).pdf`.

Using `>= maxNameRetries` as the threshold is cleaner than a magic constant — it's exactly the set of numbers the generator can never emit, so no legitimately generated counter can be misclassified. The three new table cases plus the end-to-end `report(2023)(1).pdf` case cover the behavior well.

One optional addition: `UniqueName` (the non-file path, used e.g. for dataset renames) shares `splitNameCounter`, so it is fixed by the same change — a table case there would document that, though nothing is functionally missing. LGTM from the issue side.
